text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 18 in history.
1401 - King Wladislaw II Jagiello of Poland appointed his cousin Witold Grand Prince of Lithuania.
1486 - Henry VII of England married Elizabeth, daughter of Edward IV, uniting the houses of Lancaster and York.

1689 - Charles-Louis de Secondat, baron de la Brede et de Montesquieu, French political philosopher, born. Famous for his outstanding work on political theory "L'Esprit des lois" which took 14 years (1734-1748) to finish.
1701 - Frederick III of Brandenburg was crowned Frederick I, King of Prussia.
1779 - Peter Mark Roget, English philologist, born. Creator of the thesaurus of English words and phrases that bears his name.
1841 - Emmanuel Chabrier, French composer and pianist, born. Best known for his orchestral rhapsody "Espana" and his opera "Le roi malgre lui".
1849 - Sir Edmund Barton, Australian statesman and the country's first prime minister in 1900, born.
1862 - John Tyler, 10th president of the United States (1841-1845), died. He was the first vice-president to succeed to the office after the incumbent's death.
1871 - William I of Prussia proclaimed the first Emperor of Germany in the hall of mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.
1882 - Alan Alexander Milne, English writer and creator of "Winnie the Pooh", born.
1892 - Oliver Hardy, U.S. star of music hall and screen, born. In films from 1914, but famed as half of the Laurel and Hardy double act.

1904 - Cary Grant, U.S. actor, born in England as Archibald Alexander Leach. Famed for his debonair and sophisticated appearances in such films as "Notorious", "North By Northwest" and "The Philadelphia Story".
1911 - U.S. pilot Eugene Ely became the first person to land a plane on the deck of a ship. He landed a Curtiss aircraft on a platform on the cruiser Pennsylvania in San Francisco Bay.
1913 - Danny Kaye, U.S. comedy film actor, born as David Daniel Kaminsky. Best known for his film "Secret Life of Walter Mitty". Latterly he worked for UNICEF entertaining children.
1919 - The Versailles Peace conference ending World War One opened. It was chaired by French Premier Georges Clemenceau.
1943 - In World War Two, after seven days of heavy fighting, Soviet troops relieved Leningrad after a 16-month German siege.
1954 - Sydney Greenstreet, English actor, died. Best remembered for his parts in "The Maltese Falcon" and "Casablanca".
1972 - Former Rhodesian prime minister Garfield Todd and his daughter were arrested for campaigning against the granting of legal independence to the country.
1977 - At least 80 people were killed in Sydney when a locomotive rammed a bridge bringing it crashing down on to a commuter train. It was Australia's worst rail crash.
1980 - Sir Cecil Beaton, English photographer and stage designer, died. Noted for his pictures of royalty, he also won Oscars for his costumes for the films "Gigi" and "My Fair Lady".
1991 - Iraq fired at least eight missiles at Israel in a bid to drag the Jewish state into the Gulf War the day after the allies had launched operation "Desert Storm".
1995 - Silvio Berlusconi handed over to Italy's new prime minister, Lamberto Dini.
1995 - The European Parliament endorsed the new 20-strong European Commission, in a vote marking the Strasbourg-based assembly's political coming of age.
1996 - Greece's ruling socialist party elected Costas Simitis, an avid party reformer, to replace its ailing founder Andreas Papandreou as prime minister.
